css_specificity_conflicts.issue: Duplicate .tag selector with conflicting declarations: first block (font-size 0.65rem, padding 0.2rem 0.5rem) is overridden by the second block (font-size 0.75rem, padding 0.3rem 0.7rem). The earlier block is dead code and creates maintenance confusion.
Duplicate .card-footer selector with identical declarations. Redundant and signals copy-paste drift risk.

animation_performance.issue: Animating width triggers layout/repaint on every scroll frame. Replace with transform: scaleX() for compositor-only animation.
Animating top causes layout reflow. Replace with transform: translateY() to keep animation on the compositor thread.
Animating width on the splash bar causes layout thrashing. Use transform: scaleX() instead.
transition: all is broader than necessary; animating all properties can trigger unexpected layout/paint work when non-transform/opacity properties change.

js_errors.issue: text.slice(0, index) can split surrogate pairs (emoji, wide characters). This does not throw, but produces garbled text or replacement characters as the typewriter advances.

missing_error_handling.issue: Typewriter setTimeout callbacks are never cancelled. If the element is removed from the DOM or the page navigates (SPA), timers continue running and may write to detached nodes.

No :focus or :focus-visible styles are defined for .nav-links a, .btn, .back-to-top, .modal-close, or .card-link. Keyboard users lose the default focus ring or receive no visible focus indicator depending on browser defaults.

z_index_stacking.issue: .modal-overlay and .scroll-progress both use z-index: 1000. Stacking order between them depends entirely on DOM order, which is fragile if markup is reordered.
z-index: 2000 remains on the splash even after opacity: 0. pointer-events: none mitigates interaction blocking, but the element still participates in stacking context.

mobile_breakpoints.issue: Breakpoints at 1200px, 900px, 768px, and 480px provide reasonable coverage for grid, nav, hot strip, status panel, and TOC hiding.
Redundant 480px .post-layout rule repeats the 768px behavior; harmless but unnecessary.

accessibility.issue: prefers-reduced-motion is correctly respected: animations are disabled in CSS and smooth scrolling is suppressed in JS.
outline: none is applied on focus; while box-shadow provides an indicator, there is no :focus-visible variant to distinguish mouse from keyboard focus.
No skip link or ARIA landmarks are present in the reviewed files (HTML-dependent, but notable for keyboard/screen-reader navigation).
